analyst.summary: Hindustan Copper's FY26 numbers look extraordinary on the surface -- revenue +48.6% YoY, net profit nearly doubled to Rs 920.67 crore, Q4 operating margin of 54.29% -- but the company's own operational disclosures show ore production up only 6% and MIC sales up 12% YoY, meaning the overwhelming majority of that growth is copper-price pass-through, not volume or execution. The long-run capacity story (tripling ore output toward 12.2 MTPA by 2030-31) is real and strategically credible (India's only vertically integrated copper miner, National Critical Mineral Mission, KABIL), but the anchor project -- Malanjkhand's ramp to 5 MTPA -- has a specific, verifiable execution delay: the shafts are sunk but the specialised European winders/ropes needed to equip them are stuck in a failed procurement now being retendered, pushing the real capacity timeline well behind the headline. At ~51x trailing earnings and ~14x book (correcting the quant snapshot's stale 6.4% ROE input to the true current ~32-33%), the market is capitalizing a peak-of-cycle, price-driven earnings base at a peak-cycle multiple, while also betting the capacity-execution and PSU-OFS-overhang risks (government holds ~66%, an active national asset-monetisation program is underway) don't bite. Fundamentals corroborate, rather than override, the quant model's Sell.
